mechanisms.behavior: Three targets latch down independently; the bank reset lifts all three and opens their contacts. All down spots the rotating color/number. Startup resets every bank. Each contact is paralleled with its own backbox rollover. A jammed target can hold that shared input and mask the rollover; keep contacts closed until reset. No physical speed or pulse duration is inferred from animation.

mechanisms.behavior: A drained ball closes17; output9 advances it into the three-position runway.33 is the serve end, then34/35. Output10 releases a ball to the shooter lane. Start expects three balls and resets banks; the table starts33-35 occupied. Move switches with the ball: a coil does not directly actuate a remote runway sensor. A missing ball or a held drain contact can prevent a normal serve. The hand plunger is passive.
mechanisms.label: Three-ball runway and outhole reflex

mechanisms.behavior: A ball stays on the hole switch while captive; another ball can be served. Completing a color releases captive balls, or defers release to the next turn when completed in the backbox. An isolated switch closure need not eject immediately. The kick clears the local switch only as the ball leaves; a jam can leave it held.
mechanisms.label: Left captive-ball hole

mechanisms.behavior: Cabinet button energizes a dual-winding coil through K1. A normally-closed hard-wired EOS changes the winding circuit near full travel; spring return restores rest after release. Output19 enables main flippers and drops at end-of-ball/backbox phase. Synthetic paired outputs do not measure winding or EOS state. A failed EOS/contact/relay can change travel or cause heating; no virtual timing calibration is claimed.
mechanisms.label: Right main flipper

Output19 enables main flippers and drops at end-of-ball/backbox phase. Synthetic paired outputs do not measure winding or EOS state. A failed EOS/contact/relay can change travel or cause heating; no virtual timing calibration is claimed.
mechanisms.label: Left main flipper

mechanisms.behavior: One K1 relay enables both main-flipper circuits. It is owned once here and relates to both coils through explicit relay_gated relationships. The ROM raises public19 at Start and drops it before the backbox feature; these are enable states, not flipper strokes.
mechanisms.label: Shared main-flipper enable circuit

mechanisms.behavior: One retained yellow ball returns to the bottom whip arm. A right-button-driven dual-winding flipper throws it around the right guide, through the passive upper wireform gate and into four columns of three rollovers, then back to rest. Courtesy and earned shots follow bonus. The left button stops bank lamps using matrix input 8; the modern 2.0.1 script agrees, while only the older archive table incorrectly writes switch 8 from RightFlipperKey. Public output 20 remains enabled through strokes while main-flipper enable 19 is off. Factory p23 shows a relay contact in series with the whip, but the Q18-to-relay-coil harness path remains untraced; no direct relay relationship is asserted. A stuck rollover or retained target contact can mask a score; a displaced passive gate can misroute or trap the ball. Physical timing and stroke strength remain table-owned.
mechanisms.label: Retained-ball backbox bagatelle

mechanisms.behavior: Ball rotation pulses spinner4 repeatedly; lane gate5 records traversal and passively returns. It scores/collects the lit award. Neither has a controller-driven actuator; the star-button and stand-up targets likewise return mechanically, not through a solenoid callback.
mechanisms.label: Spinner lane and passive gate

mechanisms.behavior: Ball closure of the local normally-open switch causes the ROM to pulse this mechanism's own coil, confirmed in isolation. Spring return restores the assembly. A coil pulse is not a measured sensor actuation or a calibrated physical force.
